archetype.name: Dual-Threat (passing-led)
archetype.definition: A nine-year starter whose legs still bend defenses, but who this season is winning mainly as a precise, efficient passer, with scrambles rather than designed runs carrying his rushing.

report.headline: Best passing efficiency of his career, now clouded by an ankle and thinning interior line
report.take:
Lamar Jackson has opened 2026 as one of the league's most efficient passers. He ranks first among 42 qualifiers in adjusted net yards per dropback (10.74), second in yards per attempt (10.07) and third in CPOE (8.29). That is a sharp rebound from a 2025 in which his EPA per play fell to 20th and the Ravens went 6-7 with him. The profile looks more like his 2024 season than anything since: time to throw back above three seconds (3.11), pressure turning into sacks far less often, and a passing game that produces even though Baltimore runs more than the situation predicts (25th in pass rate over expected).

The production comes from accuracy and target quality more than volume. He averages only 24 attempts a game. Short throws (0-9 air yards) have gone for +0.50 EPA with a 79.6% completion rate and five of his six touchdowns. The intermediate (15 attempts) and deep (18 attempts) buckets are both strongly positive, and Zay Flowers has turned 19 targets into +1.46 EPA per target. His legs have shifted roles too. Only 6 designed runs in four games, while 107 of his 144 rushing yards came on 10 scrambles that netted 6 first downs. The running now punishes coverage rather than serving as the engine of the offense.

The numbers hide some softness. A CPOE of 8.29 is nearly double his career best (4.55 in 2024), and that will come down. Third downs have been ordinary: 34.8% conversions and near-zero EPA, though he has faced an average of 9.2 yards to go, which says early downs are leaving him in long yardage. Red-zone passing (57.1% completions, -7 CPOE) has been bailed out by four touchdowns on 14 attempts. His bad-throw rate (14.6%, 25th of 32) is in line with his career, so the high completion rate is outrunning his actual ball placement. The level is real; the exact level is inflated.

The immediate issue is health. He played only 52% of snaps in Week 4, and his coach said Monday he did not know the chances he plays Sunday. Around him, starting guard Jovaughn Gwyn (91% of snaps) is on IR, the backup center is also on IR, guard Andrew Vorhees left Week 4, and left tackle Ronnie Stanley is questionable. A quarterback who holds the ball 3.1 seconds on a bad ankle, behind a patched interior, is the scenario most likely to drag his sack numbers back toward 2025.

strengths.title: Accuracy driving historic efficiency
strengths.body: He leads all qualifiers in adjusted net yards per dropback and ranks third in CPOE, and short throws are converting at a very high rate. Some of it is real: he was 10th in CPOE in 2024 and has been above average in most seasons. But 8.29 is far beyond anything in his career, so expect the completion rate to cool while efficiency stays well above average.

strengths.title: Pressure no longer becoming sacks
strengths.body: Only 26.3% of his pressures have ended in sacks, down from 43.9% in 2025 and 42% in 2023. This is closer to his 21.5% in 2024, his best season. He still holds the ball over three seconds, so the improvement comes from escaping and throwing rather than getting it out faster. That makes it sustainable only while his mobility and the interior line hold.

strengths.title: Scrambles as a drive extender
strengths.body: Ten scrambles have produced 107 yards, six first downs and +0.48 EPA each. That is where his rushing value now lives, with designed runs a minor part of the plan. The skill is durable, but it is the part of his game an ankle injury threatens most.

concerns.title: Ankle and a patched interior line
concerns.body: He left Week 4 after 52% of snaps, and his coach could not give odds on Sunday. Starting guard Gwyn is on IR, backup center Pocic is on IR, and Vorhees and Stanley are questionable. For a passer who extends plays, reduced mobility behind weaker guards is how the sack rate climbs back toward last year's levels.

concerns.title: Completion rate outrunning ball placement
concerns.body: A 14.6% bad-throw rate ranks 25th of 32 and matches his career norm. That sits awkwardly next to a top-three CPOE. Some completed passes have been hard catches or favorable windows, and that tends to normalize.

concerns.title: Third-and-long, red-zone wobble
concerns.body: Third-down EPA is essentially zero, with an average of 9.2 yards to go, so the problem starts with early downs not keeping him on schedule. Red-zone completions are at -7 CPOE, but four touchdowns on 14 attempts have masked it. Expect the touchdown efficiency there to slip unless the accuracy catches up.

trend.note: Passing EPA has been high in three of four games (10.3, 11.9, 11.8), the outlier being a Week 2 loss to New Orleans with 15 blitzes, 3 sacks and an interception. The Week 4 number came in about half a game before the ankle. Carries have drifted down from 7 to 2.

nextGame.headline: If the ankle allows, Atlanta's run wall pushes Baltimore to his arm
nextGame.body:
Atlanta's defense ranks 8th overall and is the league's best against the run (1st in rush EPA, 2nd in explosive runs allowed). That steers opponents into the air, and quarterbacks average 273 yards a game against them (24th). That suits Jackson's current form better than his old profile: the passing game carries Baltimore anyway. Atlanta generates a modest sack rate (27th), which helps a passer holding the ball 3.1 seconds. The catch is the deep game. Atlanta is 8th in deep EPA allowed, so his 18 deep attempts' worth of big plays may have to become short and intermediate work, where Atlanta is also solid (7th in short EPA).

Availability dominates. Jackson's ankle is a true question mark, and Baltimore's interior line is down a starting guard with Vorhees and Stanley questionable. Wide receiver Chris Moore (48% of snaps) is out, which thins the receiver depth behind Flowers and Bateman. On Atlanta's side, Za'Darius Smith (concussion, 39% of snaps) left Monday's game, which would weaken an already light pass rush if he sits. Atlanta's offense is the worst in the league by EPA, with two quarterbacks listed inactive for coach's decision, so Baltimore should not need to chase points.

keyMatchups.title: Atlanta's run defense vs. his scrambles
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta allows -0.312 rush EPA, best in the league, which shuts down designed runs. His rushing value has come mostly from scrambles, which depend on coverage holding up and on his ankle. Expect a quieter rushing line.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots into a sound shell
keyMatchups.body: His deep passes have produced +0.745 EPA on a 44% completion rate. Atlanta holds deep throws to 0.03 EPA, 8th in the league, so the explosive passing may have to come from the intermediate area instead.

keyMatchups.title: Light rush vs. patched guards
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's sack rate ranks 27th, which offsets Baltimore's loss of Gwyn. Baltimore has allowed few hits on its quarterback (3rd in hit rate). If Smith misses, the interior shortfall matters less.

nextGame.watch: His Wednesday and Thursday practice status, and whether he scrambles freely early: a stationary Jackson behind backup guards is a different quarterback.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is real: a healthy Jackson in 2024 posted top-five EPA, and this season's pressure handling and target quality look like that version. What will regress is the accuracy. A CPOE near 8 with a league-average bad-throw rate should drift toward the 3-5 range of his best seasons. Yards per attempt should settle from 10 toward the high 8s, and red-zone touchdown efficiency should cool. Baltimore's run-leaning approach caps his volume around 24-28 attempts, so his weekly totals depend on efficiency rather than volume.

Rushing is the wider question. Designed runs have been rare, and an ankle injury argues for even fewer, leaving scrambles as his main rushing source. Expect rushing output nearer his 2025 level than his historical 60-plus-yard seasons until the ankle clears. The line injuries add downside to his sack rate in the coming weeks, with Gwyn out until mid-December.
swingFactors: Ankle recovery and willingness to scramble
Interior line health with Gwyn on IR

bets.lean: BAL -2.5 (only if Jackson is confirmed active)
bets.reason: Atlanta's offense is last in EPA and last in passing EPA, with its quarterback situation unsettled. A spread under a field goal looks like it is pricing in Jackson's absence. If he plays, the number is short; if not, pass.

Atlanta allows the fewest rushing EPA and the second-fewest explosive runs. Most of his rushing comes from scrambles, and the ankle threatens those first. His carries had already fallen to 2 in Week 4.

Atlanta is the league's least efficient offense and among its run-heaviest (30th in pass rate over expected). Baltimore also leans run, and Atlanta's defense is 8th in EPA. Two of Baltimore's four games went over, so this is a slight lean only.

confidence.note: Four games and 111 dropbacks, accuracy well above his career norms, and an unresolved ankle that could change both his availability and his style.
